messages:
miguel: Quick q while I'm debugging a prod flake — what are the safe/minimal steps I can take without opening a formal access ticket? specifically: tailing app logs might surface emails/IDs. can i do that from on-call tunnel or do I need an approval? @oncall-bot any runbook link?

oncall-bot: The on-call security runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-security — start there. Ephemeral access is preferred. If you're doing anything that could expose PII or secrets, follow the 'redact & audit' checklist.

sam: Short answer: you can tail logs via the ephemeral tunnel for quick triage, but always use the redaction tooling. No screenshots or Slack dumps of prod logs. If you need full traces or DB queries, open a security request.

harini: Adding specifics: use the built-in log redactor: `rbx-logs tail --service auth --env prod --redact` — that strips emails, tokens, and SSNs by default. If you must run ad-hoc grep/sed, use examples below: 
```
# tail + redact minimal
rbx-ssh --ephemeral session=oncall-<your-name> --audit yes
rbx-logs tail --service auth --env prod --redact

# manual redaction example (use only in ephemeral session, don't paste results to public channels)
grep ERROR /var/log/auth/service.log | sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,6}/<REDACTED_EMAIL>/g' | sed -E 's/([0-9]{9,})/<REDACTED_ID>/g'
```

harini: Also: never run `cat /secrets/*` or `dbcli --dump` in prod without explicit approval. All ephemeral sessions are recorded and attached to the incident ticket.

anya: If you need elevated DB read for debugging, open a request in #security-requests with: summary, minimal query, justification, TTL (how long), and the incident/trace id. Security tries to approve within 30 mins for on-call. For break-glass outside hours use the emergency escalation flow in the runbook.

security: Confirming policy: ephemeral session + redaction is allowed for triage. Persisting or exporting PII from prod to any external location is prohibited. Any elevated access must be requested and will require audit notes. We also recommend capturing only the smallest slice of logs (time window + trace id).

miguel: OK thanks. I'm going to: 1) open an ephemeral session, 2) run `rbx-logs tail --filter 'trace=abc123' --redact` and 3) if I need DB rows I'll file a request in #security-requests. I'll paste only the redacted lines here. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Ephemeral session started: session=oncall-miguel-17631 (audit: enabled). Link: https://rbx.internal/sessions/17631 — this session will be attached to ticket if you reference it.

miguel: Ran the redacted tail — looks like a null pointer in auth token parsing. here's a tiny redacted snippet: `ERROR auth: user=<REDACTED_ID> trace=abc123 msg="token parse err"` — filing request now in #security-requests with minimal query.

sam: Good approach. Please add the session link to the ticket and include the exact time window you inspected. Keeps the audit clean.

miguel: Will do. Thanks all.
